decisions.reason: Uses the log header and tool-call line to place the worker inside the host installation npm replaces; explains remove-before-link ordering, host death, GUI disconnect, and the unrecorded tool result whose outcome is preserved as unknown; rejects the random-network-failure reading without claiming every platform must crash.

Explains env-state.txt as content-present but dsh/dsh.cmd missing and dsh.ps1 stale, content ≠ install, ties the manually swapped nonstandard tree to the broken shims, and rejects hand-swapping or hand-written shims with concrete reasons including the dsh-old downgrade trap.

Grounds the remedy in repair-notes.md: external rerun of npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1 regenerating all three shims, verification via dsh --version = rc.1, checkout aligned to the matching tag with no unrelated source edits; clearly separates the recorded repair from the proposed external procedure.

States the agent should classify it as a self-upgrade and hand off, never execute in-session; external procedure stops the host first, runs the pinned install from a plain external shell (explicitly not a tool worker of the host), restarts, hard-refreshes and verifies; distinguishes inherited stop-first/pinning rules from the new refuse-inside-target rule.

Describes a pre-flight guard intersecting the command's write targets with the host's own package root, uses the 252-file version-only diff to conclude no plugin re-migration, and gives a post-upgrade checklist covering version markers, host restart/refresh, plugin loading, and backup cleanup only after verification; conclusion stays no-code-change and tag-specific.

caps.reason: Final plan explicitly refuses in-session execution and hands the user an external procedure with the host stopped first.
Final fix is the formal external pinned registry install; manual swaps and handmade shims are analyzed and explicitly rejected.
